reproduction: Forward offspring is Binomial(d-1,p), giving p_c=1/(d-1). Along a bi-infinite geodesic, off-axis branches have disjoint edge sets; each closed attachment plus surviving branch has probability (1-p)s(p)>0 for p_c<p<1, so independent Borel-Cantelli gives infinitely many distinct infinite clusters. At p=1 the tree is connected.
scope: Known regular-tree bond-percolation special case; no general Cayley-graph separation argument.

reproduction: In finite H, Russo gives d tau_p^H(x,y)/dp=sum_e P(e pivotal). With e removed, pivotality forces x-to-u and v-to-y paths in disjoint components in one of two orientations; BK bounds by tau(x,u)tau(v,y), summed as (T_p^H A_H T_p^H)(x,y), with no 1/(1-p) factor. For f=||T_p^H||, norm Lipschitzness gives f'<=||A_H||f^2<=a f^2 a.e.; integration gives f(q)<=M/(1-aM(q-p0)). Finite-volume monotone convergence then yields the same infinite-volume bilinear bound. Direct control on the 3-vertex path: d tau_p(0,2)/dp=2p and (TAT)(0,2)=2p+2p^3.
scope: Conditional on a finite l2 norm M at p0; at p0=p_c the premise is the general missing estimate.

reproduction: If unique infinite cluster exists a.s., countability and transitivity imply theta>0 at every vertex; FKG gives tau_p(x,y)>=theta^2, so T_p delta_x is not in l2 on the infinite graph. A bounded parameter q therefore cannot be unique, and the definition of p_u plus monotonicity of bounded kernels yields p_{2->2}<=p_u.
scope: Vertex-transitive Cayley graphs; does not establish p_c<p_{2->2}.

reproduction: For T_4, tau_p(o,x)=p^dist, and |S_n|=4*3^(n-1) for n>=1, so ||T_p delta_o||_2^2=1+4p^2 sum_{m>=0}(3p^2)^m. At p=3/4 it diverges although tau decays exponentially. With rho=||A||/4=sqrt(3)/2 and p_c=1/3, p_c<1/rho is automatic but p_c*4*rho=2sqrt(3)/3>1.
scope: Refutes two insufficient routes, not the parent conjecture.

reproduction: Union over self-avoiding paths is bounded entrywise by sum_{n>=0}p^n A^n. If p||A||<1 this is a bounded Neumann kernel. When p_c||A||<1 choose p in (p_c,1/||A||); L03 yields p_{2->2}>=p>p_c and p_{2->2}<=p_u. On d-regular G, ||A||=d*rho for normalized walk rho, matching Benjamini-Schramm Theorem 4's factor d.
scope: Sufficient criterion only; T_4 shows it is not necessary.

Original Benjamini-Schramm 1996 Theorem 4 states rho(G) k p<1, with rho the normalized random-walk spectral radius and k maximum degree. For a d-regular Cayley graph the condition at p_c is p_c*d*rho<1. Since 0<rho<1 implies 1/rho>1, p_c<1/rho is automatic and cannot be the cited criterion.

reproduction: The two F(a,b) length-two routes share precisely edge {e,a}; their marginals are p^2, joint p^3, and union 2p^2-p^3. Independent Bernoulli(p^2) indicators would have joint p^4 and union 2p^2-p^4. For 0<p<1 these comparisons have opposite signs, proving stochastic-order incomparability; at p=1/2 the joints are 1/8 versus 1/16.
scope: Refutes iid path replacement only; no claim about p_u.

reproduction: For each G-edge allocate M independent Bernoulli(t) slots where t=1-(1-p)^(1/M). Distinct H-routes through the edge take distinct slots; across all H-routes the assigned slot families are disjoint, hence the path indicators are independent with probabilities t^length. Independent thinning by t^(L-length) gives iid Bernoulli(t^L) H-edges. OR of all slots gives iid Bernoulli(p) G-edges and an open H-edge has an open G-route. Infinite H-cluster inclusion gives the stated p_c inequality by continuity of the inverse.
scope: The route length L and edge congestion M are explicit premises; extra G-open edges can merge H-clusters, so no p_u or nonuniqueness transfer.
